text:
alina: quick heads-up — after landing the kernel-routing tweak yesterday i'm seeing a ~18-25% tail-latency regression on our GQA path with paged KV cache enabled (blocked on p4d-16x, seqlen=2048 workload). small repro attached below.

matt: ugh, can you paste the microbench output? is this MQA or GQA only?

alina: GQA primarily, MQA shows a smaller hit (~6-8%). below is a trimmed run from the harness:

```
# ./perf_harness --model gptx-small --mode gqa --kv-layout paged --blocksize 64 --batch 8 --seq 2048
requests: 1200 total
p50: 42ms, p90: 112ms, p95: 168ms, p99: 312ms
cpu% idle: 6, gpu% util: 87
kernel-selector: picked paged_kv_kernel_v2 most of the run
cache-frag: 0.12 (fragmentation metric)
```

jose: interesting — yesterday's selector change favors the newer 'pagedeep' kernel when avg_prefix < 256, but that heuristic may not account for high-seqlen GQA hot paths. did we change the fallback hysteresis?

matt: i bumped the hysteresis window to 5 samples in the PR to avoid flip-flop. might be keeping a suboptimal kernel sticky when seq distribution changes.

kai: can you dump the kernel pick timeline? i want to see when it switches during the run.

alina: pasted timeline snippet from the debug log:
```
[00:00:01] pick pagedeep_v2 (score 0.78) samples=7
[00:00:12] pick pagedeep_v2 (score 0.80) samples=7
[00:00:35] pick pageshallow_v1 (score 0.65) samples=2
[00:01:10] pick pagedeep_v2 (score 0.77) samples=6
```

perf-bot: nightly/harness/gqa/p4d-16x/17498 -> regression detected: p95 +22% vs baseline (17470). Details: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/17498

jose: hypothesis: pagedeep_v2 has better utilization for medium prefixes but its mem layout interacts poorly with the KV cache block allocator at blocksize=64 for large seqlen, causing more page faults / strided loads. we should try blocksize=32 and 128 to map sensitivity.

matt: agree, also try lowering hysteresis to 2 to let the selector test alternatives faster. but be careful with oscillation. we should add a sticky cool-down after a kernel swap: when a kernel is chosen because of load, keep it for at least N batches unless perf degrades by >X%.

alina: ran quick sweep:
```
blocksize=32 -> p95: 138ms (improvement)
blocksize=64 -> p95: 168ms (current)
blocksize=128 -> p95: 172ms (worse, likely cache thrash)
```

kai: that suggests smaller page block reduces fragmentation and helps prefetch locality for pagedeep_v2. can we autotune blocksize per model/seq-profile? add a metric: cache-hit-rate and mem-bound cycles.

jose: we can add quick autotune: run short microbench sets at deploy time for each model variant to pick blocksize and kernel preference. keep a per-model table: {seqlen_bucket -> preferred_kernel, blocksize}.

matt: caution — autotune needs to be cheap and non-blocking on rollout. implement as background profiler task that updates a hint store, not the global selector. runtime should read hints but still respect safety (hysteresis + rollback).

alina: i'm going to push two things: (1) a temporary revert of hysteresis bump to 2 and a 10-batch cool-down after kernel victory, (2) a model-level hint file for gptx-small: prefer pagedeep_v2 with blocksize=32 for seqlen>=1024. i'll run the nightly harness after.

matt: sounds good. add an integration test that simulates high seqlen GQA to catch this class of regressions.

perf-bot: scheduled run: nightly/harness/gqa/p4d-16x/17499 (after changes). will report delta.

kai: also add KV cache fragmentation metric to the console per-route so we can correlate. small UI change but huge debugging wins.

alina: noted. action items: alina (push revert+hint), matt (add integration test + cooldown implementation), jose (design autotune hint table + quick microbench), kai (console metric). i'll tag followups in PRs.

matt: ping me when the run is up, i'll triage.

jose: if the autotuner works we should expand to MQA+GQA switch logic; keep it conservative first.

alina: thanks all — will post results here. :thumbsup:
